explanation: BCNF requires every determinant to be a candidate key. Here C -> B holds, but C alone is not a candidate key, so the relation violates BCNF. The setup is still compatible with 3NF because B is a prime attribute, appearing in candidate key AB. That is why A is correct and the others are not.

options.text: It violates BCNF because C determines B, but C is not a candidate key.
It violates BCNF because AB is a composite key.
It violates BCNF because every third-normal-form relation automatically violates BCNF.
It violates BCNF because B is multivalued.

prompt: A relation R(A, B, C) has functional dependencies AB -> C and C -> B. Assume the candidate keys are AB and AC. Which statement best explains why R violates Boyce-Codd normal form?
reviewConcept: BCNF can require further decomposition after 3NF when a nonkey determinant remains.
